newsitem.title: MAURITANIA: Mauritania government submits formal resignation.
newsitem.headline: Mauritania government submits formal resignation.

text.p: Mauritania's Prime Minister has submitted his government's formal resignation following the ruling party's landslide election victory, officials said.

The government of Cheikh El Afia Ould Mohamed Khouna, who submitted the resignation on Sunday, will continue running the Moslem West African country until a new administration has been formed, they added.
Political sources said the resignation looked like a formality as far as the ruling Democratic and Social Republican Party was concerned.
It won a crushing first round majority on October 11 amid cries of fraud and boosted its tally to 71 of the assembly's 79 seats in last Friday's runoffs.
Action for Change, a new party championing the rights of Mauritania's blacks and ex-slaves or their descendants, won the opposition's first seat in the assembly.

A small party supporting President Maaouya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya also won one seat and independents took the rest. Two women entered the assembly -- the first women to do so in the former French colony straddling Arab and black Africa.
Many of the independents were disgruntled ruling party supporters passed over for the party ticket.
The October 11 vote was Mauritania's first truly multi-party legislative election in its transition to democracy.
The opposition boycotted the first such election in 1992, alleging widespread fraud after Taya, who seized power in a bloodless 1984 coup, won a six-year term.
Veteran opposition stalwart Ahmed Ould Daddah, who alleged massive fraud in the October 11 first round, pulled his Union of Democratic Forces-New Era party out of Friday's runoffs.
